title: Cyrus and the Debt
premise: Rosalind Whitlock, a crash investigator haunted by the deaths of her family in row twelve, receives a calendar invitation from a handler who died three days ago — and at the appointed hour, she is abducted into a conspiracy linking the crash to a Frankfurt trading algorithm that profits from engineered disasters. Hunted by the private security firm that manufactured the tragedy, Rosalind must decide whether to expose or weaponize the one secret worth killing for: proof that row twelve was targeted, not accidental. In the end, she trades the secret to a rival power broker in exchange for the evidence that convicts the firm, choosing imperfect justice over vengeance — and finally sleeps.
about_author: Sebastian Okafor is a former financial-crimes analyst who spent six years tracing money through offshore markets before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to make them disappear.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Eighteen months after the crash, Rosalind works nights reconstructing flight data, unable to sleep in any bed. A routine audit of wreckage manifests turns up an anomaly: seat 12A was rebooked eleven minutes before departure. The beat is grief sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Her phone chimes: a meeting request from Marcus Vale, the intelligence handler who once tried to recruit her — dead since Tuesday, per the obituary she attended. The invite is set for tomorrow, 6 a.m., Gate C14. She goes anyway. Beat: dread laced with compulsion.

chapters.title: Gate C14
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. At the empty gate, men in contractor windbreakers take her before the meeting time arrives. In a black van, she learns Vale scheduled the meet posthumously as insurance — and whoever holds his encrypted drive becomes the target. Beat: cold panic under interrogation.

chapters.title: The Handler's Ghost
chapters.summary: POV: Daniel Okonkwo, Vale's estranged protégé turned private investigator. Daniel reveals Vale mailed him a key the week he died, along with a warning: 'Whitlock is the witness they can't afford.' Beat: reluctant alliance formed between strangers bound by a dead man.

chapters.title: Sixty Seconds of Silence
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Reviewing Vale's partial files, Rosalind finds a gap in air-traffic audio — sixty seconds excised around the crash. Someone on the ground knew. The emotional beat: vindication curdling into horror as accident becomes murder.

chapters.title: Meridian Solutions
chapters.summary: POV: Antagonist intro — Callum Reeve, director of Meridian's security division. Reeve learns the Whitlock woman survived the pickup and orders containment, revealing Meridian trades on catastrophe data sold to Frankfurt desks. Beat: banal, corporate evil; he checks his watch mid-order.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV: Daniel. Hiding Rosalind in a decommissioned bank vault, Daniel deciphers Vale's ledger: every disaster Meridian 'responds to' was preceded by options positions opened in Frankfurt. Row twelve wasn't collateral — it was the product. Beat: the sick clarity of pattern recognition.

chapters.title: What the Dead Man Knew
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. A hidden video file shows Vale confessing he helped build the pipeline and kept the master key — the algorithm's authentication seed — as leverage. He names his buyer: a Frankfurt fund called Halberd Capital. Beat: Rosalind realizes she now carries the secret worth killing for.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: POV: Daniel. The safehouse is burned — someone inside their circle sold them out. They escape through service tunnels as Meridian teams breach above. Beat: betrayal and adrenaline; Daniel suspects his own informant network.

chapters.title: The Broker's Offer
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. A Halberd intermediary contacts Rosalind directly: sell the seed, receive wealth and erasure. She stalls, buying time, but understands both sides will kill her once the trade closes. Beat: temptation weighed against self-preservation.

chapters.title: Twelve Names
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Cross-referencing passenger lists, Rosalind finds row twelve held a whistleblower scheduled to testify against Meridian's parent company. The crash had a single intended victim — her family sat beside him by chance. Beat: rage, and the first honest mourning.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens in Nine Hours
chapters.summary: POV: Daniel. The seed expires at market open — built-in obsolescence forces a sale within nine hours or it becomes worthless. Daniel proposes leaking everything publicly instead; Rosalind knows a leak means Meridian destroys the evidence chain first. Beat: strategy under a ticking clock.

chapters.title: The Turncoat
chapters.summary: POV: Daniel. Daniel confronts his informant — a young analyst he mentored — and learns Meridian has her brother detained. He lets her go rather than break her, costing the team their early-warning line. Beat: mercy as tactical wound.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. En route to a neutral exchange point, their car is rammed on a rain-slick motorway. Rosalind survives by doing what she knows: reading the road like flight data, predicting the second vehicle's line. Beat: competence as survival; grief repurposed as instinct.

chapters.title: Reeve's Cathedral
chapters.summary: POV: Reeve. Captured and brought before Reeve in a converted church serving as Meridian's London office, Rosalind is offered the same deal as everyone else — or a quiet disappearance. Reeve speaks of crashes as 'liquidity events.' Beat: face-to-face with corruption's polite voice.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Feigning cooperation, Rosalind hands over a doctored seed while Daniel exfiltrates Vale's full archive to a magistrate and two journalists simultaneously. The real deadline shifts: survive until the story breaks. Beat: the con within the con, terror managed minute by minute.

chapters.title: Markets Open
chapters.summary: POV: Multiple, intercut. Frankfurt opens; Halberd executes on the false seed and triggers its own fail-safes, torching millions. Meridian's board scrambles as the archive hits the wire. Beat: chaos as consequence — the machine devouring itself.

chapters.title: Loose Ends
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Reeve, deniable and furious, comes for Rosalind personally rather than accept exposure. A final confrontation in the airfield hangar where the black vans first took her. Beat: the hunted becoming the hunter; justice attempted outside the law.

chapters.title: Cyrus
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Revealed: Cyrus was Vale's codename for the archive itself — and for the promise that truth outlives its keepers. Rosalind chooses not to kill Reeve, delivering him to the magistrate instead, because death would make him a martyr and silence the trial. Beat: restraint as the hardest victory.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV: Daniel. Months later, hearings begin. Daniel testifies; Meridian's executives fall; Halberd dissolves into regulatory fog — imperfect justice, but real. He visits Vale's grave and leaves the drive's last uncorrupted copy. Beat: weary catharsis.

chapters.title: What Survives
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Rosalind returns to the crash site meadow where memorials stand. She reads all twelve rows' names aloud, including the whistleblower's, then plants something growing where nothing grew. Beat: grief transmuted into remembrance without absolution.

chapters.title: First Light
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Final scene: Rosalind asleep through the night for the first time in eighteen months, waking to morning light and a life no longer defined by row twelve. A letter arrives offering her a role reforming aviation oversight. She says yes. Beat: earned peace, forward-looking close.
